inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deploys and migrations on request with no stated scope limits beyond naming a service or migration.
The prompt instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation instead of enforcing a structural approval or provenance control.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can reach the assistant
controls.decay_rationale: SSO access restriction is enforced outside the model and does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Cloud audit logging of production actions under engineer identity
controls.decay_rationale: Logging persists regardless of model capability, but it records only the shared human identity and not distinct agent provenance.

controls.name: Chat transcript retained as request record
controls.decay_rationale: Chat history is outside the model, but engineers can delete it so it does not restore attributable provenance.

controls.name: Tamper evident action provenance separating agent actions from engineer identity
controls.decay_rationale: A bound agent action record enforced outside the model would restore attribution and nonrepudiation even if the model or user cooperates with misuse.

controls.name: Immutable request and approval record that engineers cannot delete
controls.decay_rationale: An append only request record would preserve what was asked and why the action occurred, preventing loss of attribution through chat deletion.

findings.title: Missing attributable provenance for production actions performed under the engineer's personal identity

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start, so production actions are executed under the engineer's identity rather than a distinct agent identity.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, which prevents separating what the engineer did directly from what the agent did on the engineer's behalf.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, so attribution depends on a deletable record rather than a bound action provenance trail.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the request record that would explain the action can be removed after the fact.

The prompt instructs the agent to deploy services or run migrations in production using the engineer's credentials and to avoid confirmation, increasing the importance of attributable records for consequential actions.

recommendations.action: Issue the agent a distinct service identity or attach nonforgeable agent-acting-on-behalf-of metadata to each production action so audit logs distinguish agent actions from direct human actions.
Store an immutable append only request and rationale record bound to each deployment or migration event; chat history should not be the sole source of attribution.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if unattended step limits or runtime increase, or if logging or chat retention settings change; risk remains high because current detective controls do not restore attribution.

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration can be executed without a nonrepudiable request record

attack_path.note: Authenticated engineer request reaches migration action.
Agent runs production database migration using the engineer's delegated credentials.

evidence.observation: The assistant is reachable only by on call engineers, so the source is the authenticated principal's own request rather than untrusted outside content.
The agent uses the engineer's personal access token for production actions, so the migration runs as the engineer and not under a distinct agent identity.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making cap.db_migrate an irreversible consequential capability.
The only explanatory record is deletable chat history, so later review cannot reliably prove what was requested when an irreversible change occurs.
The prompt directs the agent to run named migrations in production and not ask for confirmation, leaving no structural check on a severe action.

recommendations.action: Require a tamper evident action provenance record and immutable request binding for each production migration.
Introduce a separate agent or workflow identity for production actions instead of reusing the engineer's personal token.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if the assistant gains more unattended execution or if existing logs or transcript retention are reduced; current residual stays moderate because no preventive provenance control exists today.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe self modification, tool mutation, or configurable runtime changes by the agent itself in this design.
The design contains no external egress or data disclosure path; it performs production actions rather than exporting information.
The artifacts do not state step limits, runtime limits, or queueing limits for repeated deploy or migration requests.
The artifacts do not say who can read chat transcripts or whether transcript storage is isolated from other engineers.
Loss of transcript availability is not described as a service stopping condition for production actions in the provided artifacts.
The artifacts state that cloud audit logs exist but do not describe immutability, write protections, or retention controls.
The artifacts do not describe who can read audit logs or whether logs expose sensitive deployment or migration details.
Audit log availability is not described as a prerequisite for the assistant to perform deployments or migrations in this design.

rating.rationale: Manual validation against the schema and validation checklist was applied because scripts could not run. Present risk is dominated by a high property finding: consequential production actions are performed under the engineer's personal identity, while the only explanatory record is deletable chat history, so attribution and nonrepudiation are weak. No present forecast trigger raises the tier above residual because the main gap is already structural and currently unmitigated.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No runtime configuration, identity policy, or audit retention configuration was provided, so the effectiveness and immutability of logging controls could not be verified.
No source code or orchestration config was provided, so unattended step limits, session isolation, and exact action provenance fields are not confirmed.
